title: Licence, contributions, and what a public repository says about you

videos.script: Making a repository public publishes more than the code. It publishes the terms on which anybody may use it, your name and e-mail address on every commit, and when you worked. {{more}} Most of that is decided by default, which means by nobody. A repository with no licence is not free to use. A commit made with your personal address carries it forever. {{default}} So decide each one on purpose. The licence, the address on your commits, and what a small project says about contributions it is not really expecting.
